title: Save & quit silently throws away the world when an IndexedDB write fails (no error shown, unsaved chunk edits lost)
files: src/game.js:749-784 (quitToTitle: errors at 763-777 are only console.warn'ed, then _detachWorld() + destroy)
src/ui/ui.js:415-423 (saveAndQuit always shows the title screen)
src/game.js:366 (autosave failures only go to console.error)
src/world/storage.js:431-471 (memory fallback when IndexedDB is unavailable: one console.warn only; nothing in src/ui reads storage.persistent)
evidence:
Step file tools/out/qa/savefail.json (in the snapshot), URL index.html?autostart=1&seed=42&save=1. I placed 5 stone blocks, then replaced storage._b.putChunks with a function that rejects with DOMException QuotaExceededError, then called the real UI path g.ui.openPause(); await g.ui.saveAndQuit().
Result: {state:'title', screen:'title'}. The console only shows '[game] saving the world failed: QuotaExceededError' and '[game] unloading the world failed: ...'.
Screenshot tools/out/qa/savefail-title.png shows the normal title screen with no warning.
After restoring putChunks and reopening the world, the 5 cells read [0,0,0,0,0]: the edits are gone.
The meta transaction (saveWorldMeta) had committed before the chunk write failed, so inventory and position from that session persist while its block edits do not.
expected: When saving fails, the player is told and the world stays loaded, with options to retry or quit without saving. In Minecraft a failed save is reported, not silently discarded. A browser with no usable IndexedDB should show a visible 'worlds will not be saved' warning.
actual: quitToTitle() swallows both rejections, detaches and destroys the World (dropping the only copy of the modified chunks) and returns to the title as if everything was saved. Autosave failures and the memory-only storage fallback are likewise reported only in the console.
suggestedFix: In quitToTitle(), if saveWorld() or world.destroy() rejects, keep the World attached (do not call _detachWorld) and show an error screen ('无法保存世界：<reason>' with [重试] / [不保存并退出]); only detach after success or explicit confirmation. Have World.destroy() support a 'discard' mode for the second option. Surface autosave failures with game.addChatMessage('§c自动保存失败…'). When storage.persistent === false, show a persistent warning on the title and world-list screens. Make the save atomic (see CODE-2) so a failed chunk write cannot leave a newer meta behind.
repro: node tools/harness.mjs --url "index.html?autostart=1&seed=42&mode=survival&nomusic=1&save=1" --wait-for "window.__ready" --sleep 1500 --allow-errors --steps tools/out/qa/savefail.json
verifyReasoning:
Re-ran the QA repro (tools/out/qa/savefail.json). saveAndQuit returned {state:'title', screen:'title'}, the title screen showed no warning (tools/out/qa/savefail-title.png), and after reopening the world the 5 edited cells read [0,0,0,0,0]. The only signals were two console.warn lines.

My own variant (E:/playground/minecraft/tools/out/snap-w1/tools/out/vcode/savefail2.json) also gave 9 diamonds just before quitting. After reopening, the inventory still had the 9 diamonds but the blocks were gone. So meta was written first (game.js:743) and chunks failed (744), leaving an inconsistent save.

The code confirms the rest:
- quitToTitle (game.js:762-777) swallows both rejections, then calls _detachWorld() and destroys the only in-memory copy. World.destroy() documents that on failure 'the data stays in memory (call save() again to retry)', and the integrator ignores that contract.
- ui.saveAndQuit always shows the title.
- Autosave failures only go through _logOnce (console.error).
- Nothing in src/ui reads storage.persistent or storage.backend (grep), so the memory fallback is invisible to the player.

Caveat: an IndexedDB write failure is uncommon (quota, I/O, connection closed). Blocked site storage (indexedDB.open fails, so the memory fallback is used) is the more realistic trigger. The failure is silent and permanent, so 'major' is defensible, though one could argue minor.
refinedFix:
The proposed fix is incomplete: World.destroy() sets _closing=true and removes every chunk mesh from the renderer BEFORE it saves. A World whose destroy() rejected is frozen (update() returns early) and invisible, so 'keep the World attached after destroy() rejects' would not work.

Do instead:
(1) In quitToTitle, `await this.saveWorld()` first, using the atomic snapshot from CODE-2. On rejection, do NOT detach or destroy: keep state 'playing' (paused), reset _quitting, and rethrow.
(2) ui.saveAndQuit catches that and shows a MessageScreen '无法保存世界：<err.message>' with [重试] (calls saveAndQuit again) and [不保存并退出] (calls game.quitToTitle({discard:true})). It must not call showTitle unconditionally.
(3) Only after a successful save (or with discard) call world.destroy({save: !discard}). Its internal save then finds nothing modified. Make destroy() do the mesh removal and _closing only after the save resolves, or support save:false.
(4) Autosave/hide-save failures: game.addChatMessage('§c自动保存失败：' + err.message) and retry after ~5 s instead of 30 s.
(5) When game.storage.persistent === false, show a persistent red notice on the title, world-list and create-world screens ('无法访问浏览器存储，世界不会被保存').
(6) Write meta and chunks in one transaction (CODE-2) so a failed chunk write cannot leave a newer meta behind.
leadNote: FIXER + WORLD (game/world side) and CONTAINERS (SaveFailedScreen: 重试 / 返回游戏 / 不保存并退出).
integratorNote: INTEGRATOR wave 2: game side (FIXER: world kept open, saveFailed rejection) + UI side (CONTAINERS: SaveFailedScreen with 重试 / 返回游戏 / 不保存并退出) + world side (destroy({save:false}), failed final save keeps the world usable). containers-savefail.json passes on the integrated build (the only console.error is the simulated QuotaExceededError).

title: Closing or reloading the tab keeps the inventory but loses all block edits since the last autosave (non-atomic unload save, no beforeunload guard)
files: src/game.js:732-746 (_saveNow: saveWorldMeta in its own transaction first; chunk transactions only after several awaits in world.save())
src/ (no 'beforeunload' anywhere; navigator.keyboard.lock is only used in fullscreen, src/ui/menus.js:134-140)
evidence:
Step file tools/out/qa/unload.json, URL index.html?autostart=1&save=1.
2 s after entering the world (after the initial save) I set 4 blocks in 4 different chunks ((40|56|72|88,100,40)), added 7 diamonds, then navigated away (location.href = location.pathname).
On the next page I read IndexedDB directly: meta.player.inventory = [[261,7,0]], so the meta written by the pagehide/visibilitychange save committed. storage.loadChunk() returned null ('no-chunk') for all 4 chunks, so the chunk transactions never committed.
The page is torn down after the first transaction; _saveNow issues the chunk writes only after awaiting the meta transaction.
expected: A page close, refresh or navigation either persists everything since the last save or nothing, so the state stays consistent; leaving with unsaved changes asks for confirmation. Minecraft saves the world when the window closes.
actual: The inventory, position and time are saved but recent block edits are not. Mined ores reappear while their drops stay in the inventory (item duplication), and placed blocks vanish after their items were consumed (item loss). Exposure is up to 30 s of unpaused play: the autosave timer only runs while unpaused and opening the pause menu (Esc or Alt-Tab lock loss) does not save. Ctrl, the default sprint key, plus W is a browser-reserved close-tab shortcut that preventDefault cannot block outside fullscreen keyboard lock, so sprinting can close the tab, and there is no beforeunload prompt.
suggestedFix: (1) Add Storage.saveSnapshot(meta, chunks) that writes the meta and all modified chunk records in ONE readwrite transaction over ['worlds','chunks'] (IndexedDB transactions are atomic), and use it for autosave, quit and unload. (2) In pagehide / visibilitychange 'hidden', encode synchronously and create the transaction synchronously inside the handler using the already-open IDBDatabase (no await of _storageReady or _getDB() first), then call tx.commit(). (3) Save when the pause menu opens. (4) While a non-temporary world has unsaved changes (world.stats().modified > 0 or a dirty meta), register a beforeunload handler that calls preventDefault() so Ctrl+W, Ctrl+R and tab close prompt.
repro: node tools/harness.mjs --url "index.html?autostart=1&seed=42&mode=survival&nomusic=1&save=1" --wait-for "window.__ready" --allow-errors --steps tools/out/qa/unload.json  -> metaInv [[261,7,0]], blocks ['no-chunk' x4]
verifyReasoning:
Reproduced, and the outcome is racy. I tested with a variant harness that can really close and reload tabs in the same profile (E:/playground/minecraft/tools/out/snap-w1/tools/out/vcode/harness-v.mjs).

- QA navigation repro (tools/out/qa/unload.json): 5/5 runs gave metaInv [[261,7,0]] with all 4 chunks 'no-chunk'.
- Real tab close (Target.closeTarget, tools/out/vcode/close.json and close2.json), 11 runs total: 2 had the same inconsistent state (inventory saved, zero chunk records), 1 saved nothing, 8 saved everything.
- Page.reload / F5 (tools/out/vcode/reload.json, reload2.json): 2/2 saved nothing, not even the meta, although putWorld had started inside pagehide.
- Control: an explicit await saveWorld() wrote all 4 blocks, so the chunk save itself works.

Root cause, as the finding says: _saveNow awaits the meta transaction's completion (a new task) before world.save() creates any chunk transaction. Batches of 16 are also awaited one after another. And the pagehide save is queued on _saveChain behind the visibilitychange save, so it never runs.

Other sub-claims checked in code:
- The autosave timer only advances while unpaused (game.js:363).
- PauseScreen / setScreen never save (ui.js:262-266, menus.js:570-577).
- There is no beforeunload handler anywhere in src/.
- sprint = ControlLeft/ControlRight (input.js:32), and keyboard.lock is only used in fullscreen (menus.js:134-140). I could not test Ctrl+W headless, but Chrome/Edge reserve it for closing the tab.

Closing the tab is the most common way to stop a browser game, so 'major' is right.
refinedFix:
Fix (2) as written slightly misattributes the cause. Microtask awaits inside the handler are harmless; what loses the data is waiting for a transaction to complete (a new task) before creating the next one, plus the pagehide save being chained behind an in-flight save.

Do:
(1) Add World.collectSaveRecords(): synchronously encode every READY+modified chunk plus _unloadSaves, recording editCounts. Add Storage.saveSnapshot(worldId, meta, records): ONE db.transaction(['worlds','chunks'],'readwrite'), put meta + all chunk records, then tx.commit(). Clear the modified flags (editCount compare) and the _unloadSaves entries only on complete. Use it for autosave, quit and unload.
(2) In visibilitychange 'hidden' and pagehide, call a synchronous _saveSnapshotNow() that bypasses _saveChain and creates the transaction in the same task with the cached open IDBDatabase (do not wait for a pending save).
(3) Save when the pause menu opens, as Minecraft's integrated server does ('Saving and pausing game...').
(4) While a persisted world has changes since the last successful snapshot, register beforeunload → e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue=''. This makes Ctrl+W (pressed while sprinting with Ctrl), Ctrl+R and tab close prompt first.
(5) Optionally write the meta together with the background unload-chunk saves too, so a crash cannot persist mined blocks without the matching inventory.
leadNote: FIXER + WORLD: every save uses World.saveSnapshot (one IndexedDB transaction, created synchronously in visibilitychange/pagehide); pause menu saves; 169/169 chunks persisted on real tab close.

title: No per-world session lock: a second tab on the same world silently overwrites progress with its stale state
files: src/game.js:732-746 (_saveNow writes the in-memory meta unconditionally)
src/game.js:998-1005 (a backgrounded or closed tab saves on visibilitychange/pagehide)
evidence:
Step file tools/out/qa/twotabs.json. A same-origin iframe stands in for a second tab and opened the same world from the list: {sameWorld:true}, no warning.
Tab 1 gained 30 diamonds, moved to (100.5, 120, 100.5) and saved; the stored meta became inventory [[261,30,0]], position (100.5, 100.5).
Tab 2 then ran saveWorld(), which its pagehide/visibilitychange handler does when that tab is closed or hidden; CODE-2 shows the meta write commits even on page close. The stored meta became inventory [] and position (7.5, 7.5).
Realistic trigger: a forgotten background tab holding the world gets closed after the player has made progress in a newer tab.
expected: As with Minecraft's session.lock, a world that is open in another tab cannot be opened again ('该世界已在另一个标签页中打开'), or at least a stale instance cannot overwrite a newer save.
actual: Both instances run the same world and the last one to save wins, rolling back inventory and position and potentially chunk data without any notice.
suggestedFix: In startWorld, take an exclusive Web Lock for the world: navigator.locks.request('webcraft-world-' + meta.id, { ifAvailable: true }, (lock) => lock ? holdUntilQuit : null). Refuse to open the world when the lock is unavailable and release it in quitToTitle. As a second safeguard, store a monotonically increasing meta.saveSeq and refuse to write if the stored saveSeq is newer than the one this instance loaded (optimistic concurrency).
repro: node tools/harness.mjs --url "index.html?autostart=1&seed=42&mode=survival&nomusic=1&save=1" --wait-for "window.__ready" --sleep 500 --allow-errors --steps tools/out/qa/twotabs.json
verifyReasoning:
The QA iframe repro gave {sameWorld:true}, stored inventory [[261,30,0]] at (100.5,100.5), and then [] at (7.5,7.5) after the second instance saved.

I also checked the realistic case with real tabs (E:/playground/minecraft/tools/out/snap-w1/tools/out/vcode/twotabs3.json, multi-tab steps in harness-v.mjs):
1. Tab A plays the world.
2. Tab B opens the same world from the list with no warning, gains 30 diamonds, moves, and does 保存并退出 (stored meta: 30 diamonds at 100.5,100.5).
3. I close the forgotten tab A without calling saveWorld manually.

In 3/3 runs, A's pagehide/visibilitychange save rolled the stored world back to an empty inventory at (7.5,7.5).

Note: removing an iframe is NOT a valid proxy for a tab close (no overwrite happened in that variant), but real tab close reproduces reliably.

There is no navigator.locks, BroadcastChannel or saveSeq anywhere in src/. _saveNow only checks state === 'playing', which a backgrounded tab still has.

The trigger needs the same world open in two tabs, which is plausible since the world list puts the last-played world first. Severity sits between minor and major; the data loss is silent.
refinedFix:
The proposed Web Locks fix is right. Hold the lock for the whole session: in startWorld, `const ok = await new Promise(res => navigator.locks.request('webcraft-world-' + meta.id, { ifAvailable: true }, lock => { if (!lock) { res(false); return; } res(true); return new Promise(r => { this._releaseWorldLock = r; }); }));` and throw new Error('该世界已在另一个标签页中打开') when !ok. Call this._releaseWorldLock() at the end of quitToTitle, after the final save. The lock is released automatically if the tab dies.

For the optimistic-concurrency safeguard, read and compare the stored meta.saveSeq INSIDE the same readwrite transaction as the write (the CODE-2 snapshot transaction), and abort if the stored value is newer. A separate read-then-write would itself race.

Optionally, the world list can mark worlds whose lock is held (navigator.locks.query()) as '已在其他标签页中打开'.
leadNote: FIXER: per-world WorldLocks (Web Locks + BroadcastChannel fallback); a second tab can neither open nor delete the world.

title: Torches can't be attached to walls; clicking a wall's side either does nothing or places a floor torch in front of it
files: src/world/registry.js:159-165 (hasSupport only looks at the block below), 289-309 (getPlacementBlock has no wall variant)
src/game/interaction.js:368-382 (_placementCell), 397 (support check uses world.getBlock(x, y - 1, z))
src/world/blockupdates.js:117-129 (support re-check only against the block below)
evidence: Real right-clicks on a flat world (steps file tools/out/qa/place2.json, run with index.html?autostart=1&seed=1&type=flat&mode=survival). 'TORCH on side of wall': target {x:24,y:7,z:-2,face:4,stone}, cell (24,7,-1) stays 'air' and the torch count is unchanged. 'TORCH on side of wall at floor level': target {x:24,y:4,z:-2,face:4}, a free-standing torch appears at (24,4,-1) and isn't attached to the wall. tools/out/qa/walltorch.json repeats this on a cobblestone wall at night: clicking the face at y=6 gives cell 'air' with all 10 torches kept; clicking at y=4 places a 'torch' and leaves 9. Screenshot tools/out/qa/walltorch.png shows the torch standing on the grass in front of the wall.
expected: Minecraft: right-clicking the side face (N/S/E/W) of a block with a sturdy face places a wall torch attached to that face, angled away from the wall. This works at any height and doesn't depend on the floor. The torch pops off when the block it's attached to is removed. Wall torches are the normal way to light caves and tunnels.
actual: The clicked face is ignored for torches. Placement succeeds only when the cell below the target cell is a solid cube, and then it produces a free-standing floor torch. Otherwise it silently fails. Torches can't be put on cave walls, pillar sides or ceilings-adjacent walls.
suggestedFix: Add hidden wall_torch_{north,south,east,west} variants (item 'torch', lightEmission 14, same selection-box style) with a new placement type 'wall' in getPlacementBlock. face 2 gives the standing torch; faces 0/1/4/5 give the wall variant facing the face normal; face 3 is rejected. Make the support check for wall variants test the block behind (x - nx, z - nz) for a solid cube instead of the block below, in both Interaction.placeBlock and BlockUpdater._check. BlockUpdater must also enqueue the 4 horizontal neighbours on a change so wall torches pop when their wall is broken. Add the leaning torch geometry to the mesher (Minecraft: about 22.5° tilt, base offset 5/16 toward the wall).
repro: 1) index.html?autostart=1&seed=1&type=flat&mode=survival. 2) __game.debug.give('torch',10); build a stone column at (24,4..8,-2); stand at (24.5,4,0.5). 3) Aim at the wall's south face at y≈7.5 and right-click: nothing happens. 4) Aim at the face at y≈4.5 and right-click: a standing torch appears on the floor in front of the wall.
verifyReasoning:
I reproduced this with real right-clicks in the snapshot: E:/playground/minecraft/tools/out/snap-w1/tools/out/vp/wt1.json on index.html?autostart=1&seed=1&type=flat&mode=survival, with a cobblestone wall at z=-3, y=4..7 and 10 torches.
(A) Target {x:0,y:6,z:-3,face:4}: cell (0,6,-2) stays 'air', the inventory still holds 46x10, and there is no feedback at all (wt1_a.png).
(B) Target {x:1,y:4,z:-3,face:4}: a standing 'torch' appears at (1,4,-2) and the inventory drops to 46x9. wt1_b.png shows it as an upright post on the grass in front of the wall, not attached to it.
(C) Removing the wall block behind it leaves the torch in place, as expected for a floor torch.
(D) Clicking the underside of a block at y=7 (face 3) also does nothing.

The code explains it. getPlacementBlock (registry.js:289-309) has no wall variant and returns the plain torch for every face. interaction.js:397 checks support only at (x, y-1, z). hasSupport('solid') (registry.js:163) needs a solid cube below. BlockUpdater._check (blockupdates.js:117-129) and blockChanged (62-66) look only at the cell below / the cell above. All cited lines match.

No doc lists this as a deliberate deviation. SPEC §7 defines only the standing torch geometry, and SPEC asks for Minecraft-faithful choices where it is silent. Wall-mounting torches is one of the most common Minecraft actions, and here it fails silently. Major severity is defensible. No capability is lost, though: floor torches still light caves.

The suggested fix is right in principle. Two details are off: 'face 3 is rejected' doesn't match Minecraft, and the leaning geometry and selection box are imprecise (see refinedFix).
refinedFix:
1) Registry: append 4 hidden variants `wall_torch_north/south/east/west` (variant() of torch, so item 'torch' and lightEmission 14). Ids 95-128 are already reserved by SPEC-wave2 §1, so append after them (e.g. 129-132). Give them a new placement type and a 'wall' support kind that records the attachment direction.
2) Placement should follow Minecraft's StandingAndWallBlockItem. Build a direction list: the opposite of the clicked face first, then the player's nearest looking directions; skip UP. DOWN gives the standing torch if the block below is a solid full cube. A horizontal direction d gives the wall torch facing -d if the block at cell+d is a solid full cube. Take the first candidate that can survive, otherwise fail. In practice: side faces 0/1/4/5 attach to the clicked block, face 2 gives a standing torch, and face 3 falls back to an adjacent wall or the floor (don't simply reject it).
3) Replace hasSupport(id, below) with canSurvive(world, x, y, z, id). Use it in Interaction.placeBlock and in BlockUpdater._check. BlockUpdater.blockChanged must also enqueue the 4 horizontal neighbours, so a wall torch pops (dropping 'torch') when its wall is broken.
4) Mesher: use Minecraft's template_torch_wall. The post spans [-1,3.5,7]..[1,13.5,9]/16, rotated -22.5° about the wall-parallel axis with the pivot at the wall face (0, 3.5/16, 8/16). The foot touches the wall 3.5 px up and the top leans about 3.8 px outward. Rotate per facing.
5) Selection box: 5 px deep from the wall, e.g. facing north = [5.5,3,11, 10.5,13,16]/16.
6) Flame particles: block centre + 0.27 toward the wall, y + 0.92 (WallTorchBlock.animateTick). Update particles.js:527, which only knows BLOCK.TORCH.
leadNote: Wave 2: lead (wall-torch variants 129-132, canStay, getPlacementBlock), SURVIVAL (placement with Minecraft fallbacks), WORLD (support popping + wall-torch mesh model).

title: Default sprint key Ctrl + W closes the browser tab in windowed mode with no confirmation, losing up to 30 s of unsaved progress
files: src/game/input.js:30-33 (sprint bound to ControlLeft/ControlRight), 278-286 (_shouldBlockKey: preventDefault can't cancel the reserved Ctrl+W)
src/game.js:38 (AUTOSAVE_SECONDS = 30), 990-1006 (only an async saveWorld() on visibilitychange/pagehide)
src/ui/menus.js:128-143 (Keyboard Lock only in fullscreen), 533 (loading tip)
evidence: Sprint is bound to ControlLeft/Right, matching Minecraft's default. Chrome/Edge reserve Ctrl+W (also Ctrl+T/Ctrl+N), so keydown.preventDefault() can't stop the tab closing outside fullscreen with navigator.keyboard.lock. docs/notes/player.md lists this as a known limitation. grep -r beforeunload src/ finds nothing, so nothing intercepts the close. Saves happen only every 30 s plus a fire-and-forget async IndexedDB write in pagehide that the browser may cut off. The only mitigations are the fullscreen button and a loading-screen tip. This can't be reproduced in headless CDP because browser accelerators aren't triggered there; the evidence is the code plus documented browser behaviour.
expected: Holding Ctrl and then pressing W is a standard way to sprint in Minecraft. The web game shouldn't vanish when the player does it. At minimum, while a world is open, the browser should ask 'Leave site?' before closing.
actual: In a normal (non-fullscreen) window, the first time a player holds Ctrl and presses W, or stops and re-presses W while Ctrl is held, the tab closes immediately. Ctrl+T (sprint + chat) opens a new tab the same way. Blocks placed or mined since the last autosave may be lost.
suggestedFix: While state === 'playing', register a beforeunload handler: window.addEventListener('beforeunload', (e) => { if (game.world && game.state === 'playing') { game.saveWorld(); e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = ''; } }) and remove it on quitToTitle. Chrome then shows a confirmation for Ctrl+W instead of closing. Optionally also offer a toggle-sprint or rebindable sprint key in Options, and show the Ctrl+W tip once in-game (chat or action bar) the first time sprint is triggered with Ctrl in windowed mode.
refinedFix:
1) In Game._attachDomListeners (game.js ~989), add:
window.addEventListener('beforeunload', (e) => { if (this.world && this.state === 'playing' && !this.options?.automation) { this.saveWorld().catch(() => {}); e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = ''; } });
Chrome shows 'Leave site?' only after sticky user activation, which every real player has. The harness's Browser.close skips beforeunload, and the automation guard keeps tests unaffected.
2) Make the unload save robust. On pagehide, write the meta plus ALL dirty chunks in ONE IndexedDB transaction, issued synchronously inside the handler (e.g. a World.saveAllSync() that encodes every modified chunk and calls a single putChunks). Today the batches are chained with awaits, and the page dies after the first one.
3) Optional: add an Options toggle for sprint mode or a rebindable sprint key. Show the Ctrl+W tip in-game (action bar) the first time Ctrl-sprint is used outside fullscreen.
leadNote: FIXER: beforeunload 'Leave site?' dialog while unsaved progress exists; SURVIVAL: one-time tip recommending double-tap W on the first Ctrl-sprint outside fullscreen.

title: Closing or reloading the tab loses everything since the last autosave: the pagehide/visibilitychange save never reaches IndexedDB
files: src/game.js:997-1006 (visibilitychange / pagehide handlers call async saveWorld())
src/game.js:732-746 (_saveNow: await saveWorldMeta(meta) then await world.save())
src/world/world.js:973-990 (_saveAll awaits _flushUnloadSaves, then writes 16-chunk batches one after another)
src/world/storage.js:323-346, 412-417 (each put is a separate async transaction with no commit())
evidence: Without the fix: 0 of 25 edits and 0 chunk records survived a reload done 3 s after the edits, and 0 of 25 survived closing the browser 5 s after the edits (persistent profile, fixed origin). With a 32 s wait (so the autosave ran first), 25 of 25 survived. A trace (tools/out/qa/abrupt-steps-trace.json) shows that during unload saveWorldMeta starts ('meta-start@5028'), 'meta-done' never appears, and storage.saveChunks is never called. The world meta is lost as well (tools/out/qa/abrupt-meta-steps.json): after the reload, lastPlayed is 4266 ms older than the reload, time is 1000 instead of 20000, player y is 79 instead of 140, and the 33 diamonds given just before the reload are missing. Fix probe: a pagehide handler that synchronously opens ONE readwrite transaction over ['worlds','chunks'], puts the meta plus encodeChunkRecord() for every modified chunk and calls tx.commit() kept 25 of 25 edits, 27 chunk keys and a fresh lastPlayed (1.5 s) (tools/out/qa/fixprobe.mjs + fixprobe5-steps.json). The same code without tx.commit() lost everything (fixprobe6). It also lost everything when queued behind the game's own uncommitted async 'worlds' transaction (fixprobe3). A chunks-only synchronous transaction with commit() worked (fixprobe2).
expected: SPEC §9.10 says 'Autosave every 30 s and on quit / visibilitychange hidden'. Closing the tab, pressing F5 or closing the browser should keep block edits, player position, inventory and time, just as Minecraft saves when the window is closed.
actual: Everything since the last 30 s autosave is silently discarded: blocks, position, inventory, time and the world-list order (lastPlayed). Autosave also stops while the pause menu is open, so 'pause, then close the tab' loses everything since the last autosave.
suggestedFix:
Add a synchronous unload path and call it from pagehide and from visibilitychange (hidden) instead of the async saveWorld():
1. World.collectUnsaved() returns the modified READY chunks plus the _unloadSaves entries.
2. Storage.saveAllSync(worldId, meta, chunks) uses the already-open IDBDatabase (IDBBackend._db) to create one transaction(['worlds','chunks'], 'readwrite', {durability:'relaxed'}) inside the event handler. It puts the meta and encodeChunkRecord(blocks) for each chunk, then calls tx.commit().
3. Clear the modified flags only in oncomplete, and use a flag so the two events issue only one write.
4. Do not start the async meta save first: the sync transaction must not queue behind an uncommitted readwrite transaction on 'worlds'.
